description: Sync rows from every table in the Airtable bases you choose, one document per row. Airtable permissions are not imported.
opening: Sync the rows of every table in the Airtable bases you select. Each row is one document, with its field values written as labelled lines of text. A linked-record field links the row to the rows it references. Attachment file names are searchable, and a file's text can be added when it can be downloaded and read.

Airtable permissions are not imported, so every synced row is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. You cannot pick single tables: every table in a selected base is synced. A row's date is when it was created, not when it was last edited. Rows deleted in Airtable stay in HydraDB.

synced.text: Give every field in a table a distinct name. Field names are lowercased and their spaces and punctuation simplified before they are written. Two fields whose names then match can overwrite each other, and a field whose name becomes `id` can replace the record id that identifies the row.

notes: Airtable base and workspace collaborators, sharing and interface permissions are not reproduced. Set an access rule on each base that must be restricted.
Every synced row carries `additional_metadata.rbac_warning`, a notice that Airtable collaborators were not captured.

connect.auth: Airtable uses a personal access token.

credentials.name: token
credentials.text: An Airtable personal access token with the scopes below and access to the bases you want synced.

connect.credentials_note: Personal access tokens do not refresh. To rotate one, create a replacement with the same scopes and bases, update the connector, check that the bases still list and sync, then revoke the old token.

permissions.name: data.records:read
permissions.text: reads the rows of each table.

permissions.name: schema.bases:read
permissions.text: lists bases, their tables and their fields.

connect.permissions_note: Scopes alone do not open a base. Add every base you want synced to the token.

steps.title: Create a personal access token
steps.text: In Airtable, create a personal access token with `data.records:read` and `schema.bases:read`.

steps.title: Give it your bases
steps.text: Add every base you want synced to the token.

steps.title: Select bases
steps.text: HydraDB lists the bases the token can reach. Select the bases to sync. Every table in a selected base is synced. To reach rows older than 30 days, raise `lookback_days` when you select them.

connect.account: One connector reads the bases one personal access token can reach.

sync.first_sync: Each selected base reads back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default, measured by each row's last modified time.
sync.changes: Each sync reads every table in the base and picks up the rows modified since the last sync.
sync.edits: A modified row is sent again and replaces its document. A formula or rollup value that changes because of another table, or because time passed, does not count as a modification of the row. It stays out of date until the row itself is edited.
sync.deletes: Deleted rows are not removed. A row deleted in Airtable stays searchable in HydraDB.

documents.name: Rows
documents.one_document: One row of a table in a selected base.
documents.title: The row's field named `name`, `title` or `subject`. Otherwise the first non-empty field in alphabetical order, skipping linked-record fields. A row with none is titled `Airtable record` and its id.
documents.text: The title, then one line per non-empty field in alphabetical order, as the field name in title case and its value. Lists are joined with commas. An object shows its name, title, text, file name, email or URL. An attachment field shows file names only. Linked-record fields are left out of the text, because they become graph connections. Numbers are written with at most six decimal places. Fields are searchable as text, not as separate filters.
documents.date: When the row was created. Airtable rows carry no last-edited time.
documents.files: Files in attachment fields are downloaded and read when they are hosted by Airtable, can be downloaded and are of a supported type. A file that is missing, too large or unsupported keeps only its name in the row text.

attributes.name: Attachments
attributes.text: File names in the row text, plus the text read from each file that could be read.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the row was created. Used as the result date, so ranking by date reflects creation, not the last edit. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The table as base id and table id joined by a colon. Limits a query to one table, and stays the same when the table is renamed. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The table name. Limits a query to one table by name. Two tables can share a name, so use the id keys to tell them apart. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.airtable_base_id
attributes.text: The base id, which starts with `app`. Limits a query to one base. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.airtable_table_id
attributes.text: The table id. Limits a query to one table by id. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.rbac_warning
attributes.text: A notice that Airtable collaborators were not captured. Present on every row. It neither grants nor denies access. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's rows. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Linked records
attributes.text: Each linked-record field links the row to the rows it references, across tables in the same base. The field is not kept as searchable text. Not searchable.

example_searches: Which rows in the Customers table are on the Enterprise plan?
What is the status and owner of the Website relaunch project?
Which tasks are linked to the Q3 Launch project?

connections: A row to each row it references through a linked-record field, across tables in the same base.
No links to items in other tools.
people: No people are attached. Collaborator, user and person fields are written as text, by name or email.
graph.from_text: Every field value in the row's text, and the text read from attached files.

not_synced: Rows last modified before the `lookback_days` window on the first sync.
Comments on records and revision history.
A link back to the row in Airtable.
Deletions: deleted rows stay in HydraDB.
